metadata.title: Jack Strand struggles in relief action on Sunday
metadata.description: Jack Strand completed 8 of 15 passes for 59 yards with a pick-six and a fumble in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also ran twice for 16 yards.
metadata.analysis: Strand got off to a rocky start with a pick-six three plays after he came in relief duty for the benched Cooper Rush. It will be tough to trust Strand or Rush at any point moving forward if the offense needs to rely on them.

metadata.title: Jack Strand - Shows little in relief of Rush
metadata.description: Strand completed just eight of 15 passes for 59 yards and an interception in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Cooper Rush was benched after going 10-for-17 passing with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Strand came on in relief and was just as ineffective. The 22-year-old is an undrafted rookie who played his college football at tiny Minnesota State-Moorhead, so it's no surprise he wasn't ready for the NFL in his first regular-season game action. With Michael Penix (knee) potentially back for Thursday night's game at Green Bay, Strand will be a cut candidate. Strand would make more sense on the practice squad where he can learn in a no-stress environment.

metadata.title: Jack Strand Makes Regular-Season Debut vs. Panthers
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons rookie quarterback Jack Strand made his regular-season debut in Week 2 after entering Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons were down 34-3 in the third quarter, with Cooper Rush completing 10 of 17 passes for 86 yards and two interceptions. Strand played in three preseason games for Atlanta, completing 24 of 36 passes (66.7% completion rate) for 306 yards with one touchdown pass and one interception. The 22-year-old had a 63.8% completion rate over four seasons playing at Minnesota State Moorhead with a 126:50 TD:INT ratio.

metadata.title: Jack Strand - Backup QB again Sunday
metadata.description: Strand is listed as the No. 2 quarterback for Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: With Michael Penix (knee) out and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) doubtful, Cooper Rush (back) will start again in Week 2. While Strand is currently penciled in as the No. 2 signal-caller against Carolina, he'll see action if Rush is forced to miss any time.

metadata.title: Jack Strand to serve as backup QB for Falcons in Week 2
metadata.description: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Jack Strand will be the backup quarterback again on Sunday against the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: It will be Cooper Rush drawing another start with Michael Penix Jr. ruled out and Tua Tagovailoa listed as doubtful.

metadata.title: Jack Strand - Could be an option in Week 2
metadata.description: Strand could be an option for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The Falcons' injury woes at quarterback could lead to Strand being active and available again in Week 2. Not only are Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix (knee) dealing with injuries, but Cooper Rush is also getting treatment for his back. Tagovailoa was not practicing Wednesday, while Rush was expected to be a full participant. Penix was throwing off to the side. Depending how the injury reports shake out over the coming days, Strand could be the backup yet again for the Falcons as they host the Panthers.

metadata.title: Jack Strand - Backup QB for Week 1
metadata.description: Strand will serve as the Falcons' backup quarterback behind Cooper Rush for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The Falcons chose to carry four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, and that looks to have been a savvy move after Tua Tagovailoa was ruled out for Week 1 due to an oblique injury he sustained in Thursday's practice. With Michael Penix (knee) also sidelined, the Falcons will turn to the veteran Rush to start under center while Strand -- an undrafted rookie out of Minnesota State-Moorhead -- operates as the QB2. Strand played in all three of the Falcons' preseason games, completing 24 of 36 passes for 306 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning 17 carries into 29 yards and two scores.

metadata.title: Jack Strand to be backup QB for Falcons Sunday
metadata.description: Jack Strand will enter Sunday's season opener for the Falcons as the backup quarterback.
metadata.analysis: Tua Tagovailoa was ruled out with an oblique injury. Cooper Rush will get the start as a result.

metadata.title: Jack Strand - Makes roster as one of four QBs
metadata.description: Strand is one of four quarterbacks who made Atlanta's 53-man roster, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: The three QBs to make the roster along with Strand are Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix Jr. (knee) and Cooper Rush. Strand is listed as last on the team's initial depth chart, so he's unlikely to see much action, if any, barring injuries to multiple signal-callers ahead of him. Falcons GM Ian Cunningham called the team's decision to carry four quarterbacks "a little bit of an insurance policy," per the Associated Press, in acknowledgement of Tagovailoa's injury history and the knee issue Penix is still working his way back from. Still, Strand -- who signed with Atlanta as an undrafted free agent in May -- could ultimately end up on the practice squad when/if the team needs to provide more depth at other positions.

metadata.title: Jack Strand takes all 11-on-11 reps at Falcons practice Friday
metadata.description: Jack Strand took all of the 11-on-11 reps at Falcons training camp on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Strand continues to work with the starters as Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa ease their way back from injuries. Penix took reps in 7-on-7 drills on Friday.
